sections.title: Section 1: Causes and Background of the Swadeshi Movement

questions.q: The immediate cause of the Swadeshi Movement was:
questions.sol: The Partition of Bengal (1905) by Lord Curzon was the immediate cause of the Swadeshi Movement.

questions.q: The Partition of Bengal was announced on:
questions.sol: The Partition of Bengal was announced on July 20, 1905 by Lord Curzon.

questions.q: The stated reason for the Partition of Bengal was:
questions.sol: The British claimed administrative efficiency as the reason, but the real motive was divide and rule.

questions.q: The real motive behind the Partition of Bengal was to:
questions.sol: The real motive was to weaken the growing nationalist movement by dividing Bengalis along religious lines.

questions.q: The Swadeshi Movement was formally proclaimed at:
questions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement was formally proclaimed at a massive protest meeting at Calcutta Town Hall on August 7, 1905.

questions.q:
Consider the following underlying causes of the Swadeshi Movement:
1. Growing nationalist sentiment
2. Dissatisfaction with Moderate methods
3. Influence of international events
4. Gandhi's return to India
Which are correct?
questions.sol: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Gandhi was NOT in India during the Swadeshi Movement; he was in South Africa.

questions.q: The Partition of Bengal divided the province into:
opts: East Bengal and Assam, and West Bengal
questions.sol: The Partition created East Bengal and Assam (with Dhaka as capital) and West Bengal (with Calcutta as capital).

questions.q: October 16, 1905 was observed as:
questions.sol: October 16, 1905, the day the Partition came into effect, was observed as a day of mourning throughout Bengal.

questions.q: The Rakhi Bandhan ceremony was introduced to symbolize:
questions.sol: The Rakhi Bandhan ceremony was introduced by Rabindranath Tagore to promote Hindu-Muslim unity.

questions.q: Which international events influenced the Swadeshi Movement?
questions.sol: The Boer War and Russo-Japanese War influenced Indian nationalists by showing that Asian powers could defeat European ones.

sections.title: Section 2: Methods and Strategies of the Swadeshi Movement

questions.q: The four pillars of the Swadeshi Movement were:
questions.sol: The four pillars were Swadeshi, Swaraj, Boycott, and National Education.

questions.q:
The boycott during the Swadeshi Movement included:
1. British goods
2. British courts
3. British schools
4. British government services
Which are correct?
questions.sol: All four were part of the boycott - British goods, courts, schools, and government services.

questions.q: The Bengal National College was established in:
questions.sol: The Bengal National College was established in 1906 as part of the National Education movement.

questions.q: Who was the first principal of Bengal National College?
questions.sol: Aurobindo Ghosh was the first principal of Bengal National College.

questions.q: Tilak started which festivals for mass mobilization?
questions.sol: Tilak started the Ganapati and Shivaji festivals to mobilize masses and spread nationalist sentiment.

questions.q: The Swadeshi Movement used which methods for mass mobilization?
questions.sol: The movement used traditional festivals, melas, folk songs, poems, and street plays for mass mobilization.

questions.q: The economic aspect of the Swadeshi Movement included:
opts: Promotion of Indian goods and industries
questions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement promoted Indian goods and industries, including textile mills, soap factories, and matchbox factories.

questions.q:
The National Education movement emphasized:
1. Education in vernacular languages
2. Science and technology
3. Indian culture
4. British literature only
Which are correct?
questions.sol: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The movement emphasized vernacular languages, science, technology, and Indian culture.

questions.q: Public bonfires during the Swadeshi Movement were of:
questions.sol: Public bonfires of foreign (British) cloth were a prominent feature of the Swadeshi Movement.

questions.q: The Swadeshi Movement involved which sections of society?
questions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement involved students, women, and common people along with the urban middle class.

sections.title: Section 3: Key Leaders and Their Contributions

questions.q: Who gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright'?
questions.sol: Bal Gangadhar Tilak gave the famous slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'.

questions.q: Who was known as the 'Lion of Punjab'?
questions.sol: Lala Lajpat Rai was known as the 'Lion of Punjab'.

questions.q: Bipin Chandra Pal edited which newspapers?
questions.sol: Bipin Chandra Pal edited newspapers like 'Bande Mataram' and 'New India'.

questions.q: Who composed the 'Vandemataram' song that became the anthem of the Swadeshi Movement?
questions.sol: Rabindranath Tagore composed the 'Vandemataram' song that became the anthem of the Swadeshi Movement.

questions.q:
Match the following leaders with their regions:
A. Tilak - 1. Bengal
B. Bipin Pal - 2. Maharashtra
C. Lajpat Rai - 3. Punjab
D. Aurobindo - 4. Bengal
questions.sol: Tilak (Maharashtra), Bipin Pal (Bengal), Lajpat Rai (Punjab), Aurobindo (Bengal).

questions.q: Surendranath Banerjee edited which newspaper?
questions.sol: Surendranath Banerjee edited 'The Bengalee' newspaper.

questions.q: Who among the following was a Moderate leader who supported the Swadeshi Movement?
questions.sol: Surendranath Banerjee was a Moderate leader who supported the Swadeshi Movement.

questions.q: Lala Lajpat Rai founded which organization in America?
questions.sol: Lala Lajpat Rai founded the Indian Home Rule League in America.

questions.q: Aurobindo Ghosh later became a:
questions.sol: Aurobindo Ghosh retired from politics and later became a spiritual leader.

questions.q: The newspaper 'Kesari' was run by:
questions.sol: Kesari (Marathi) and Mahratta (English) were newspapers run by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

sections.title: Section 4: Impact and Legacy of the Swadeshi Movement

questions.q: The Swadeshi Movement is considered the first mass-based political movement because:
opts: It involved students, women, and common people
questions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement was the first to involve masses including students, women, and common people.

questions.q:
The economic impact of the Swadeshi Movement included:
1. Growth of textile mills
2. Establishment of soap factories
3. Matchbox factories
4. Heavy industries
Which are correct?
questions.sol: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The movement led to small-scale indigenous industries, not heavy industries.

questions.q: The Swadeshi Movement gave rise to which parallel strand?
questions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement gave rise to revolutionary terrorism as young Indians adopted violent methods.

questions.q: Which revolutionary groups emerged during the Swadeshi period?
questions.sol: Anushilan Samiti and Yugantar were revolutionary groups that emerged during the Swadeshi period.

questions.q: The Partition of Bengal was annulled in:
questions.sol: The Partition of Bengal was annulled by King George V at the Delhi Durbar on December 12, 1911.

questions.q: The annulment of the Partition of Bengal is considered a partial victory because:
opts: The capital was shifted to Delhi
questions.sol: It was a partial victory because while the partition was annulled, the capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.

questions.q: The Swadeshi Movement laid the foundation for:
questions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement laid the foundation for Gandhian mass movements by introducing methods of mass mobilization.

questions.q: The political impact of the Swadeshi Movement included:
opts: Shift from Extremist to Moderate politics
Shift from Moderate to Extremist politics
questions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement marked the shift from Moderate to Extremist politics.

questions.q: The concept that became central to Indian nationalism after the Swadeshi Movement was:
questions.sol: The concept of Swaraj (self-rule) became central to Indian nationalism after the Swadeshi Movement.

questions.q: The Muzaffarpur bombing case (1908) involved:
questions.sol: The Muzaffarpur bombing case involved young revolutionaries Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki.

sections.title: Section 5: Decline and Reasons for the Swadeshi Movement

questions.q: The Swadeshi Movement began to decline around:
questions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement began to decline around 1907-1908 due to various factors.

questions.q:
Which of the following were reasons for the decline of the Swadeshi Movement?
1. British repression
2. Surat Split
3. Arrest of Tilak
4. Gandhi's call to withdraw
questions.sol: Statements 1, 2 and 3 were reasons. Gandhi was not involved in the Swadeshi Movement.

questions.q: Tilak was deported to Mandalay in:
questions.sol: Tilak was deported to Mandalay (Burma) in 1908 for 6 years of exile.

questions.q: The Surat Split (1907) weakened the Swadeshi Movement because:
questions.sol: The Surat Split weakened the movement by dividing Moderates and Extremists.

questions.q:
The British response to the Swadeshi Movement included:
1. Arrests of leaders
2. Press censorship
3. Banning public meetings
4. Police brutality
Which are correct?
questions.sol: All four were part of the British repression - arrests, press censorship, banning meetings, and police brutality.

questions.q: The social base of the Swadeshi Movement was limited to:
opts: Urban middle class, students, and professionals
questions.sol: The movement's social base was primarily the urban middle class, students, and professionals.

questions.q: The Muslim League was formed in 1906 with British support as part of:
questions.sol: The Muslim League was formed in 1906 with British support as part of their divide and rule policy.

questions.q: The Surat Split occurred because Moderates wanted to:
questions.sol: Moderates wanted to limit the Swadeshi and Boycott movement to Bengal, while Extremists wanted nationwide expansion.

questions.q: After the decline of the Swadeshi Movement, many young Indians turned to:
questions.sol: After the decline, many young Indians turned to revolutionary methods and terrorism.

questions.q: The lack of proper organizational structure was a weakness of the Swadeshi Movement because:
questions.sol: The movement relied on charismatic leadership and lacked proper organizational structure to sustain a long-term movement.
